messages.author: 2922d38dc6c70170
messages.subject: non-symmetric CIs for SEM models
parts:
Hi all,

I was wondering if there is any way to get non-symmetric CIs for the parameters in a model built using lavaan's the SEM command?

I know I can get symmetrical ones using commands like:

parameterestimates(fit.comb, boot.ci.type = "bca.simple", standardized = T)

but I am wondering if there is a way to allow the CIs to be asymmetrical.

Thank you!

-Michael

messages.author: 13deaaee5806ffce
messages.subject: Re: non-symmetric CIs for SEM models
parts:
Hi Michael,

Before calling parameterestimates(), you may run something like
fit.comb <- sem(your.model, data=your.data, se="bootstrap", bootstrap=1000)

messages.subject: Re: non-symmetric CIs for SEM models
parts:
Michael,

The difference between ML and MLR is only in fit statistics and SEs. Since you're not using the ML/R SEs, using ML won't make any difference to the bootstrap results.

Pat

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: non-symmetric CIs for SEM models
parts: but I am wondering if there is a way to allow the CIs to be asymmetrical.

Bootstrapping is one way.  The Monte Carlo method is another (see the ?semTools::monteCarloMed help page).  I was under the impression Carl Falk was working on profile likelihood confidence intervals for lavaan a while back, but that was several years ago and my memory might betray me there; regardless, AFAIK, they are not yet a feature provided by lavaan.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen
